# `silk/simd/cpu`

<!-- Generated by silk doc-reference. Do not edit by hand. -->

Runtime detection of the CPU features that the running machine has, to choose a kernel at
run time.

## When to use
Use [`CpuFeatures.available`](#CpuFeatures.impl.available) when one binary must pick a faster kernel on machines that have
a feature the build does not select. Use `Target.hasCpuFeature` with `static if` when the
build itself selects the feature, which costs nothing at run time.

## Details
A [`CpuFeatures`](#CpuFeatures) value is a set of feature names of the target architecture, spelled as in
the compilation profile, such as `"avx2"`, `"dotprod"` or `"simd128"`. [`CpuFeatures.selected`](#CpuFeatures.impl.selected)
is the set the build selects. [`CpuFeatures.machine`](#CpuFeatures.impl.machine) is the set the running machine has, which
always includes the selected set:

- x86-64 reads `cpuid`, and counts AVX and AVX-512 features only when the operating system
  saves their registers (`xgetbv`).
- AArch64 Linux with GNU libc reads `getauxval`. AArch64 Darwin reads `sysctlbyname`.
- wasm32 cannot ask the engine, and other profiles cannot ask the system, so they report
  the selected set.

The first question in a process asks the machine and keeps the answer, so later questions
cost one memory read. [`CpuFeatures.available`](#CpuFeatures.impl.available) answers for one feature named at compile time:
it is `true` at compile time when the build selects the feature.

A kernel that uses a feature's instructions is an `unsafe fn` compiled with `@features`.
Calling it is safe once `available` answered `true` for each of its features.

## Gotchas
- A name from another architecture, or an unknown name, is never present.
- A detected feature does not make `Target.hasCpuFeature` true, also inside a function with
  `@features`. Such a function calls the feature's `Intrinsic` operations itself.

## Examples
### Choose a kernel at run time
```silk
import silk.simd.cpu { CpuFeatures }
import silk.num.u64

static if Intrinsic.targetArchitecture() == "x86_64" {
  @features("popcnt")
  unsafe fn countFast(value: u64) -> u32 {
    return u64.countOnes(value)
  }
}

fn count(value: u64) -> u32 {
  static if Intrinsic.targetArchitecture() == "x86_64" {
    if CpuFeatures.available("popcnt") {
      return unsafe countFast(value)
    }
  }
  return u64.countOnes(value)
}

pub fn main() -> i32 {
  if count(255) != 8 {
    return 1
  }
  return 0
}
```

### Compare the machine with the build
```silk
import silk.simd.cpu { CpuFeatures }

pub fn main() -> i32 {
  let machine = CpuFeatures.machine()
  let build = CpuFeatures.selected()
  // The machine has every feature the build selects.
  if !CpuFeatures.containsAll(&machine, &build) {
    return 1
  }
  if CpuFeatures.has(&machine, "no-such-feature") {
    return 1
  }
  return 0
}
```

## `CpuFeatures`

```silk
pub struct CpuFeatures
```

A set of CPU features of the target architecture.

### When to use

Use [`CpuFeatures.available`](#CpuFeatures.impl.available) when one binary must pick a faster kernel on machines that have
a feature the build does not select. Use `Target.hasCpuFeature` with `static if` when the
build itself selects the feature, which costs nothing at run time.

### Details

The names are spelled as in the compilation profile, such as `"avx2"`, `"dotprod"` or
`"simd128"`. [`CpuFeatures.selected`](#CpuFeatures.impl.selected) is the set the build selects. [`CpuFeatures.machine`](#CpuFeatures.impl.machine) is
the set the running machine has, asked once per process, and always includes the selected set.

### Gotchas

- A name from another architecture, or an unknown name, is never present.
- A detected feature does not make `Target.hasCpuFeature` true. Code that uses the feature's
  instructions must still be compiled for it, in an `unsafe fn` with `@features`.

<a id="CpuFeatures.impl.machine"></a>

### Associated function `machine`

```silk
pub fn machine() -> CpuFeatures
```

Returns the features of the running machine, which include [`CpuFeatures.selected`](#CpuFeatures.impl.selected).

#### Details

The first call in a process asks the machine and keeps the answer in process-wide storage,
so later calls cost one memory read:

- x86-64 reads `cpuid`, and counts AVX and AVX-512 features only when the operating system
  saves their registers (`xgetbv`).
- AArch64 Linux with GNU libc reads `getauxval`. AArch64 Darwin reads `sysctlbyname`.
- wasm32 cannot ask the engine, and other profiles cannot ask the system, so they report the
  selected set.

Threads that call it at the same time may each ask the machine once. They get the same
answer.

#### Gotchas

A detected feature does not make `Target.hasCpuFeature` true. Code that uses the feature's
instructions must still be compiled for it, for example in an `unsafe fn` with
`@features`.

<a id="CpuFeatures.impl.detect"></a>

### Associated function `detect`

```silk
pub fn detect() -> CpuFeatures
```

Returns the features of the running machine, asking it again on every call.

#### When to use

Use [`CpuFeatures.machine`](#CpuFeatures.impl.machine), which asks once per process. Use `detect` only where a cached
answer must not be used.

#### Details

The result is the same set that [`CpuFeatures.machine`](#CpuFeatures.impl.machine) returns, and includes
[`CpuFeatures.selected`](#CpuFeatures.impl.selected). Asking the machine can take thousands of cycles in a virtual
machine.

<a id="CpuFeatures.impl.available"></a>

### Associated function `available`

```silk
pub fn available(static name: string<'static>) -> bool
```

Returns `true` if the running machine has the CPU feature `name`, to choose a kernel at run
time.

#### When to use

Use it in front of an `unsafe fn` compiled with `@features(name)`: call the function only
when this returns `true`.

#### Details

When the build selects `name` (`Target.hasCpuFeature`), the answer is `true` at compile
time and costs nothing. Otherwise it reads the answer that [`CpuFeatures.machine`](#CpuFeatures.impl.machine) keeps,
which is one memory read and one bit test after the first call in the process. On wasm32
and other profiles that cannot ask the machine, it is `false` at compile time.

#### Gotchas

A name from another architecture, or an unknown name, is never available.
